1-1.title: Prime Factorization
1-1.contentObjective: I can write a number as a product of its prime factors using a factor tree.
1-1.languageObjective: I can explain how I broke a number down using the words prime number, composite number, factor, and exponent.

vocabulary.definition: A number bigger than 1 that you can only divide by 1 and itself.

vocabulary.definition: A number bigger than 1 that you can divide by more than just 1 and itself.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número mayor que 1 que se puede dividir entre más números, no solo 1 y sí mismo.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Một số tự nhiên lớn hơn 1 có nhiều hơn hai ước.
vocabulary.definitionAr: عدد صحيح موجب أكبر من 1 له أكثر من عاملين.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir un número como números primos multiplicados.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Viết một số dưới dạng tích của các số nguyên tố.
vocabulary.definitionAr: كتابة عدد صحيح على شكل حاصل ضرب أعداد أولية فقط.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que divide exactamente a otro número, sin dejar residuo.

vocabulary.definitionAr: عدد يقسم عددًا آخر قسمة تامة بدون باقٍ.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número pequeño que dice cuántas veces multiplicar un número por sí mismo.

vocabulary.visual: 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8

1-1.workedExample:
I want the prime factorization of 60. I start by splitting it: 60 = 6 × 10.
6 is not prime, so I break it: 6 = 2 × 3. Both 2 and 3 are prime, so I stop those branches.
10 is not prime, so I break it: 10 = 2 × 5. Both 2 and 5 are prime, so I stop.
Now every factor is prime: 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.
Using exponents, I write it as 2² × 3 × 5. I check: 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60. Correct.

misconceptions.mistake: Stopping too early and leaving a composite number in the factorization, like writing 60 = 6 × 10.
misconceptions.tip: Keep breaking every branch until each number left is prime.

misconceptions.mistake: Writing 1 as a prime factor.
misconceptions.tip: 1 is not prime, so prime factors start at 2.

misconceptions.mistake: Adding the prime factors instead of multiplying them to check.
misconceptions.tip: Multiply all the primes together to see if you get the original number.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir un número como números primos multiplicados. Ayuda a encontrar el MCD.

1-2.workedExample:
I want the GCF of 24 and 36. First I list the factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24.
Next I list the factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36.
Now I circle the factors in BOTH lists: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. These are the common factors.
The biggest one is 12, so the GCF of 24 and 36 is 12. I check: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 36 ÷ 12 = 3. Both are even, so 12 works.

Then I skip count the multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24.
I look for the first number in BOTH lists. 12 is in both lists, and it comes before 24.
So the LCM of 4 and 6 is 12. I check: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 12 ÷ 6 = 2, so both go into 12 evenly.

1-4.workedExample:
I want 1,344 ÷ 12. The dividend is 1,344 and the divisor is 12.
First I take a big easy chunk: 12 × 100 = 1,200. I subtract: 1,344 − 1,200 = 144.
Now I divide 144: 12 × 12 = 144. I subtract: 144 − 144 = 0, so nothing is left.
I add my chunks: 100 + 12 = 112. So 1,344 ÷ 12 = 112.
I check by multiplying: 12 × 112 = 1,344. Correct, and the remainder is 0.

The tank has 128.75 liters. A shuttle adds 46.8 liters. I line up the decimal points and annex a zero: 46.80.
I add: 128.75 + 46.80 = 175.55 liters.
Now the thrusters use 19.35 liters, so I subtract: 175.55 − 19.35 = 156.20.
The final fuel level is 156.20 liters. I check with estimation: about 130 + 47 − 19 = 158, which is close, so my answer is reasonable.

Now Keep, Change, Flip: keep 7/2, change ÷ to ×, flip 1/4 to 4/1.
Multiply: 7/2 × 4/1 = 28/2.
Simplify: 28/2 = 14. So 3 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 14 segments.

2-5.workedExample:

6-7.title: Simplify Algebraic Expressions

vocabulary.definition: Terms with the same letter, like 2x and 5x.

vocabulary.definition: To add or subtract terms with the same letter into one.

The rooms need microphones and stands: (4 + 2 + 6) microphones and (3 + 5 + 1) stands.

misconceptions.mistake: Combining terms with different variables, like 4m and 3s.
misconceptions.tip: Add only terms that share the exact same variable.

7-1.title: Write Equations
7-1.contentObjective: I can write an equation to represent a real-world situation.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equal sign showing both sides are the same.

vocabulary.definition: The = sign, showing both sides are the same.

Clue: 'A number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.'
The unknown is the number of gems. I let n stand for it.

7-2.title: Solve One-Step Addition and Subtraction Equations
7-2.contentObjective: I can solve one-step addition and subtraction equations using inverse operations.
7-2.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words equation, inverse operation, isolate, and solution.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equal sign showing both sides are the same.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática con un signo igual que muestra que ambos lados son iguales.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Một phát biểu toán học cho thấy hai biểu thức bằng nhau.

vocabulary.definition: To get the letter by itself on one side.

vocabulary.definitionVi: Đặt biến số đứng một mình ở một bên của phương trình.

7-2.workedExample:
Solve n + 23 = 58. The 23 is added to n.
The inverse of adding 23 is subtracting 23.
I subtract 23 from both sides: n + 23 − 23 = 58 − 23.
That leaves n = 35. Check: 35 + 23 = 58. True!

misconceptions.tip: Undo the number that is added to or subtracted from the variable.

misconceptions.mistake: Skipping the check step after finding the solution.
misconceptions.tip: Put your answer back into the original equation to test it.

vocabulary.definitionAr: وضع المتغير بمفرده في أحد طرفي المعادلة.

vocabulary.definition: The number multiplied by a variable.

The inverse of multiplying by 3 is dividing by 3.
I divide both sides by 3: 3x ÷ 3 = 21 ÷ 3.

7-6.workedExample:
Solve x + 3 > 53. The inverse of adding 3 is subtracting 3.
I subtract 3 from both sides: x + 3 − 3 > 53 − 3, so x > 50.
The symbol > does not include 50, so I use an open circle at 50.
'Greater than' shades right. Check: x = 60 gives 60 + 3 = 63 > 53. True!

7-7.workedExample:
Clue: 'A total divided equally among 4 people gave each $85.'
This has an exact total, so I use an equation. Let t be the total.
Divided among 4 to get 85 means t ÷ 4 = 85, so t = 85 × 4 = 340.
Check reasonableness: $340 split 4 ways is $85 each. That makes sense!

8-1.title: Statistical Questions and Data
8-1.contentObjective: I can tell the difference between a statistical question and a non-statistical question.
8-1.languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words statistical question, data, variability, and survey.

vocabulary.definition: A question where the answers will be different for different people.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una pregunta cuyas respuestas serán distintas para distintas personas.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Câu hỏi có nhiều câu trả lời khác nhau khi khảo sát dữ liệu.
vocabulary.definitionAr: سؤال نتوقع أن تكون له إجابات متنوعة عند جمع البيانات.
vocabulary.visual: "How tall are the players on the team?" → answers vary: 60 in, 63 in, 58 in, 65 in

vocabulary.definition: Facts and numbers you collect, like answers to a survey.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Datos y números que recoges, como respuestas a una encuesta.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Các thông tin hoặc số liệu được thu thập để phân tích.
vocabulary.definitionAr: المعلومات أو الأرقام التي يتم جمعها لتحليلها.
vocabulary.visual: Player heights: 60 in, 63 in, 58 in, 65 in — four different measurements

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Mức độ khác biệt hoặc phân tán của dữ liệu.
vocabulary.definitionAr: مدى انتشار أو اختلاف القيم في مجموعة البيانات.
vocabulary.visual: Scores 10, 12, 11 are close together (low variability); scores 2, 15, 30 are far apart (high variability)

vocabulary.definition: Collecting facts by asking people questions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Recoger datos haciendo preguntas a las personas.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Hành động thu thập dữ liệu bằng cách đặt câu hỏi cho nhiều người.
vocabulary.definitionAr: طريقة لجمع البيانات عن طريق طرح الأسئلة على مجموعة من الناس.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Mô tả cách thức các điểm dữ liệu trải rộng trên một tập dữ liệu.
vocabulary.definitionAr: وصف لكيفية انتشار نقاط البيانات في مجموعة البيانات.

8-1.workedExample:
Question 1: "How many points did our top player score last night?" There is one player and one game, so there is one fixed answer, like 18 points.
One answer, no variety, so this is NOT a statistical question.
Question 2: "How many points does each player score per game?" The answers vary: 8, 12, 12, 15, 18, 20, 22.
Because the answers are different for different players, I must collect data. This IS a statistical question.

misconceptions.mistake: Thinking any question about numbers is a statistical question.
misconceptions.tip: A statistical question is one where the answers can vary, not just any math question.

misconceptions.mistake: Calling a question statistical when it has one fixed answer, like one score in one game.
misconceptions.tip: If there is only one true answer, it is not a statistical question.

misconceptions.mistake: Believing a question about many people is always statistical, even when everyone gives the same answer.
misconceptions.tip: Ask if the answers would actually be different before you decide.

misconceptions.mistake: Focusing on the word 'how many' instead of on whether the data varies.

8-2.contentObjective: I can find the mean, median, and mode of a data set.

vocabulary.definition: The average. Add all the numbers, then divide by how many there are.

vocabulary.definition: The number that shows up most often.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que aparece más veces.
vocabulary.definitionVi: Giá trị xuất hiện nhiều lần nhất trong tập dữ liệu.
vocabulary.definitionAr: القيمة الأكثر تكراراً في مجموعة البيانات.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.

vocabulary.definitionVi: Mức độ khác biệt hoặc phân tán của dữ liệu.
vocabulary.definitionAr: مدى انتشار أو اختلاف القيم في مجموعة البيانات.

8-2.workedExample:
My small data set: 2, 4, 4, 6, 9. There are 5 numbers.
Mean: add them, 2 + 4 + 4 + 6 + 9 = 25, then divide by 5. So the mean = 25 ÷ 5 = 5.
Median: the numbers are already in order. The middle (3rd) value is 4, so the median = 4.
Mode: the number 4 appears twice, more than any other, so the mode = 4.

8-3.workedExample:

10-3.workedExample:
My box is 8 long, 5 wide, and 3 tall. I unfold it into a net and see 3 pairs of faces.
Top and bottom: each is 8 × 5 = 40, and there are 2 of them, so 2 × 40 = 80.
Front and back: each is 8 × 3 = 24, so 2 × 24 = 48.
Left and right: each is 5 × 3 = 15, so 2 × 15 = 30.
I add all the pairs: 80 + 48 + 30 = 158. The surface area is 158 in².

misconceptions.mistake: Finding the area of only one face and calling it the surface area.
misconceptions.tip: Surface area is the total of all faces, so add up every face on the net.

misconceptions.mistake: Forgetting that faces come in matching pairs on a rectangular box.
misconceptions.tip: Each face has a twin, so multiply each face area by 2 before adding.

misconceptions.mistake: Multiplying the three dimensions like a volume problem.
misconceptions.tip: Surface area adds flat face areas, so multiply within each face and then add, not all three edges together.

misconceptions.mistake: Labeling the answer with cubic units instead of square units.

10-4.workedExample:
My triangular prism has triangle bases (base 6, height 4), is 10 long, and the two slant sides are 5 each.
Each triangle base is ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, and there are 2 of them: 2 × 12 = 24.
Now the 3 rectangles: 6 × 10 = 60, 5 × 10 = 50, and 5 × 10 = 50, which add to 160.
I add the bases and the rectangles: 24 + 160 = 184.
So the surface area is 184 in². I counted 5 faces because it is a triangular prism.

10-5.workedExample:
My square pyramid has a 6 × 6 base and a slant height of 8.
First the base area: 6 × 6 = 36.
Now one triangular face: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24. A square pyramid has 4 of them, so 4 × 24 = 96.
I add the base and the side faces: 36 + 96 = 132.
So the total surface area is 132 in². I used the slant height (8) for the triangles, not the pyramid's height.
